dataset_family: Single-centre local Parkinson's disease cohort, Chinese PLA General Hospital, Beijing (25 PD-MCI, 25 PD-NCI, 25 HC; cross-sectional). New, and not shared with any current supporter or other candidate.
method_family: Resting-state fMRI: voxel-wise degree centrality, with secondary seed-based FC and an ROI volume check (VBM/CAT12). rs-fMRI connectivity is the same method family as supporter P-518 (and candidate P-554).
what_it_shows: At group level, rs-fMRI degree centrality differed between PD-MCI and PD-NCI in five clusters: decreased in left fusiform/cerebellum VI and right hippocampus, increased in bilateral precuneus and left cuneus. Two of these clusters had DC correlated with MoCA, and their extracted regional volumes did not differ significantly across the three groups (F = 1.914, P = 0.155; F = 2.780, P = 0.069). The authors read this as functional abnormality appearing before structural change.
why: Stated form: PARTLY. The part it shows is a functional (connectivity) measure separating MCI from non-MCI at group level in regions whose volume did not significantly differ. What it does not show: (1) Detection in any diagnostic sense: no classifier, AUC or cross-validation. (2) Insufficiency of hippocampal or whole-brain volume. Only the two MoCA-correlated DC clusters were volume-tested (p.3). The right-hippocampus DC cluster was never volume-tested, and no whole-brain or hippocampal volumetric comparison is reported, although Methods describe a VBM of GM/WM (p.2). (3) Lateness: the design is cross-sectional, and the authors say the temporal ordering 'needs further longitudinal study' (p.5). (4) The population is PD-MCI, not AD-spectrum MCI. (5) The precuneus volume null is borderline (P = 0.069) with n = 25 per group, a pilot by the authors' own description, so this is absence of evidence. Narrowed form: PARTLY. It is the same shape as the P-518 clause (connectivity separated MCI from comparators where the tested volumes did not), but the tested volumes are the regional volumes of the functionally selected clusters, not hippocampal subvolumes, and the population is Parkinson's. Independence: new dataset. The rs-fMRI method family duplicates P-518. No shared authors or site with supporters. Not in VF-20's rejected_supporters (the finder's note of a VF-25 rejection concerns a different statement). Peer-reviewed (Neuroscience Letters 2021).

quotes.quote: Compared with the PD-NCI group, the PD-MCI group showed decreased DC in the left fusiform gyrus (FFG), left cerebellum lobule VI, and right hippocampus, as well as increased DC in the bilateral precuneus and left cuneus.

For VBM analysis, the volumes of the ROIs in which DC values were related to cognitive abilities (MoCA score) were extracted separately and entered in SPSS. Then, we eliminated the influence of age and sex on volume by regression analysis, and performed ANOVA among the three groups

However, there was no significant correlation for cluster 3 (right hippocampus) (R=0.294, P = 0.154), cluster 4 (left cuneus) (R=-0.212, P = 0.310), and cluster 5 (right precuneus) (R=-0.320, P = 0.119).

There was no significant difference among the three groups for the volumes of the two ROIs (cluster 1: left FFG/cerebellum lobule VI; F = 1.914, P = 0.155 and cluster 2: left precuneus; F=2.780, P = 0.069) that were related to cognitive abilities (MoCA score).

suggesting a functional disruption of these brain regions, but the structure is relatively normal. That is to say, functional connectivity abnormalities appear prior to structural changes. It would be tempting to hypothesize that with cognition decline progresses, brain volume would change, but this needs further longitudinal study.
First, the patient sample size was not large, and our results must be considered pilot
Third, as this was a cross-sectional study, the structural changes caused by the progress of cognitive decline have not been seen
